plan: dispatch://INFRA-234/artifact/plan-md is the whole plan. Documentation only: docs/kubernetes.md, the section 'Running a workload in the cluster from a role' (2554-2829 at base 5c182bd1), and AGENTS.md line 127. Ten tasks T1-T10, nine acceptance criteria A1-A9, each with its surface and command. Two of the issue's five findings (the reason clause and the AGENTS.md back-pointer) do not run: sjawhar/legion#2149 is OPEN, measured at plan time.

implement: legion-worker: the implementer's own part of it — the push procedure, the handoff write, the pull request it opens with 'Dispatch: INFRA-234', and the no-deferral rule.

legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the body template, the definition of a proof (surface, command, observed, head SHA, negative control), and the rule that a docs-only pull request omits the Thermo line entirely, which is why no ce-simplify-code pass is planned.
legion-worker/references/default-branch-check.md: the App-identity check on its own commits before the push.

legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md: both this pull request and sjawhar/legion#2149 edit AGENTS.md within a row of each other, so a conflict is likely and must be a forward merge, never a rebase.
legion-worker/references/findings.md: anything found outside INFRA-234 during the live run is a dispatch ask, never an issue it files.
dispatch-first and dispatch: any Dispatch write, including the measurement record of sjawhar/legion#2149's state.
envoy: reaching the architect, and the subscribe-then-end-the-turn pattern if a CI re-run has to be waited for.
ce-simplify-code: does not apply. The diff is documentation only, and pr-body.md's own rule gives a docs-only diff no simplify pass.
test: legion-worker: the tester's part — the handoff with implementerProof, failures and its own proof, and the verdict it alone carries.

legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the tester runs the application rather than CI again. Here the application is the page's own sequence, re-driven independently from a role container under a fresh six-character workload suffix, with CI read from the CI line for everything static.
dispatch-first and dispatch: any Dispatch write.
envoy: reaching the implementer or the architect with what a re-drive found.
review: legion-worker: the reviewer's part — the order of a round and the completion that ends the phase, not the review.
legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md: the read of the head's checks, the approval of the head by SHA, and what the architect's acceptance then needs.
legion-worker/references/review-threads.md: one disposition reply per thread, read before answered, resolved by the implementer and never in bulk.
legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the two lines the reviewer owns, 'Look at first' and 'Not proven / risk', and the verification of both E2E proofs against the surface they name.
dispatch-first and dispatch: any Dispatch write.

findings.finding: F1: 'the corrected manifest applied as published' — a server dry run does not retire the 'Not executed' bullet; only a real run proves the new selector, and endpoints cannot be read (can-i get endpoints is no).
findings.answer: Plan section 3, task T8: the full sequence is driven for real from a role container — Job applied, uid read, Service applied as published with the uid selector, both waits, the reachability block answering by the Service name, kubectl logs, kubectl delete job, closing listing. The two server dry runs are the negative control (T8 step 6), not the proof.

findings.finding: F2: does 'whatever is written is driven from a role container' bind the whole evidence passage, or only the sentences this issue changes?
findings.answer: Only the sentences this issue changes. Plan task T4 splits the passage into three dated bullets: what was re-driven on 2026-10-25 for this change, what was driven for dispatch://INFRA-71 on 2026-10-24 and not re-run since (the credential-less gate, the deliberate breakages, the reachability block's three synthetic cases), and the refused-as-published record. Nothing is carried forward silently under a single date.

findings.finding: F3: two more passages of the same class as findings 3 and 4 (the 'may no more list a Service' sentences at 2772-2775 and the grant matrix at 2781-2784) are false and are not among the spec's five, while the spec forbids moving any other sentence.
findings.answer: In scope. Plan task T3 corrects them, and plan section 6 records the departure with the measurement behind it (list services yes; kubectl get jobs,pods,svc exits 0). dispatch://INFRA-215's subject is the reachability check reading a refusal one way when it has two meanings, not the Services grant, so these are not its gaps. The architect is told in the completion summary.

findings.finding: F4: once the Service half really runs, the sequence's closing 'kubectl get jobs,pods' cannot show the sweep that the paragraph above the manifest promises.
findings.answer: Plan task T3 makes the closing line 'kubectl get jobs,pods,svc', which the identity may now run (measured exit 0). It is part of the same recorded departure as F3.

findings.finding: F5: a mis-selectored Service and a missing reachability label give the identical symptom (never answered: TimeoutError), so a green run does not by itself prove the corrected selector.
findings.answer: Plan task T8 step 5 adds the attribution step: before the reachability block, read the workload pod's labels and record that they carry batch.kubernetes.io/controller-uid equal to the Job's uid and the reachability label. No new sentence is added to the page: the bullet at 2638-2645 already tells a role to compare those labels.

findings.finding: F6: the private-name elision has no automated backstop, and the natural negative control quotes the admission policy's name twice.
findings.answer: Plan section 2 names three literals to elide — the reachability label's name, the admission policy's name, and the deployment's owner and its domain, with the namespace kept unwritten as the page already keeps it — gives the replacement register (quote the rule, never the policy), lists the surfaces swept (diff, commit messages, branch name, pull request title and body, review replies, every handoff, plan.md, Envoy messages), and makes the sweep a role-run grep whose patterns live in shell variables and never in a committed script, fixture or the pull request text. Measured: the tree names the deployment's owner nowhere today.

findings.finding: F7: nobody owns spec findings 1 and 2 if sjawhar/legion#2149 merges after this issue closes, and both pull requests edit AGENTS.md within a row of each other.
findings.answer: This is the one decision sent to the architect (plan section 7), with the recommendation that dispatch://INFRA-221's own pull request carry both, since it already edits both files and already writes the forward half of the cross-reference. Until it answers, the plan runs as written: the implementer re-measures once with 'gh pr view 2149 --repo sjawhar/legion --json state,mergedAt' and records the result either way.

findings.finding: F8: AGENTS.md line 127's trailing clause ('which wait on that apply') is made false by findings 3 and 4, which decouples that row edit from sjawhar/legion#2149.
findings.answer: Plan task T5 edits that clause unconditionally, so the row no longer waits on a merge it has nothing to do with. Recorded in the departure of plan section 6 as acceptance criterion A5.

findings.finding: F9: 'dated' is not yet a specification — what the date anchors to, whose run it names, and what the reader does when it is stale.
findings.answer: Plan task T4: each bullet carries an ISO date and where it ran; the passage's opening sentence says the deployment's grants change under the page and that a reader re-runs the three gate commands itself rather than trusting the recorded answers. The date is the implementer's run; the tester's independent re-drive does not re-date the page, and a different answer there is a test failure rather than an edit.

findings.finding: F10: a kubectl sequence driven from a pod has no run id and no link, which the pull-request contract assumes.
findings.answer: Plan section 4, 'Evidence form': the command stands in for the run id, the six proof fields are spelled out, 'observed' carries the outcomes with the three literals elided, and the negative control is the pair of server dry runs. The plan says plainly that no artifact store exists for a pod-driven run, so no link is claimed.

findings.finding: F11: the proof costs a shared four-processor quota under one identity every project's agents hold, and the tester's path was undecided.
findings.answer: Plan sections 3 (T8) and 5: one workload at a time, implementer then tester, never concurrent; a fresh six-character suffix per run; a hand delete and the closing listing. The tester re-drives the full sequence rather than re-reading a transcript, and the cost is stated rather than discovered. The manifests are applied as published, deadlines included, because that is the acceptance line; the worst case of an interrupted turn is one self-terminating hour.

findings.finding: F12: the conditional work needs a measurement rather than a question, and finding 1's wording cannot come from the pull request's description.
findings.answer: Plan tasks T6 and T7 give the exact command, both branches, the requirement to quote the image's clients from the merged text of the Worker image section on main rather than from the pull request description, the two existence checks before the back-pointer is written, and the machine-checkable acceptance that the exec and operator-setup clauses stay byte-identical.

findings.finding: F13: the provenance line — every claim that a sentence of the page is false rests on live measurements the analyst could not run.
findings.answer: Plan section 1 is that provenance: one table, every row a command and its result, all run from this issue's role container on 2026-10-25, and the plan attributes each measurement to that dated run rather than stating it as a timeless fact.

specDepartures.spec: 'No other sentence of that section moves: its known gaps are dispatch://INFRA-215's.'
specDepartures.plan: Tasks T3 and T5 correct two further passages and one command of the published sequence: the sentences at docs/kubernetes.md:2772-2775 claiming this identity may not list a Service, the grant matrix at 2781-2784 listing get/list/create services as 'no', the sequence's closing listing at 2751, and the trailing clause of AGENTS.md:127 saying steps wait on the apply.
specDepartures.evidence: Measured from this issue's role container on 2026-10-25: kubectl auth can-i list services / get services / create services all answer yes, and kubectl get jobs,pods,svc exits 0, where the page says it exits 1 with 'services is forbidden'. These are the same class as the spec's findings 3 and 4, sentences the same apply made false, and are not dispatch://INFRA-215's, whose subject is the reachability check reading a refusal one way when it has two meanings. Left alone, the corrected page contradicts itself twice within forty lines, and the sweep promised above the Service manifest stays unprovable because the published listing cannot see a Service.

outcome.scope: Two acceptance lines the spec does not carry, A4 (the page no longer says this identity may not list a Service, and the closing listing shows the Service went with the Job) and A5 (AGENTS.md:127 no longer says steps wait on the apply), and the scope constraint quoted above. No decision a human settled is touched.

specDepartures.spec: 'What has to be true at the end' lists the corrected reason clause and both AGENTS.md rows pointing at each other.
specDepartures.plan: Neither is delivered by this plan. Tasks T6 and T7 are conditional and, on the plan-time measurement, do not run; the implementer re-measures once and records the result either way.
specDepartures.evidence: gh pr view 2149 --repo sjawhar/legion --json state,mergedAt at plan time: state OPEN, mergedAt null; dispatch://INFRA-221's Dispatch status is in_progress. The architect's brief (dispatch://INFRA-234/comment/5f3b17b0-8f3c-47ed-9137-db898e6ccd19) directs exactly this: 'plan the three that stand and say in the plan that the other two wait'. What the brief does not settle is who carries them if sjawhar/legion#2149 merges after this issue closes, which plan section 7 sends to the architect with a recommendation.

acceptance: The reason clause states what is true after the tool half merged, and names which of the sentence's three reasons changed — conditional, and not met on the plan-time measurement.
Both AGENTS.md rows point at each other — conditional, and not met on the plan-time measurement.
outcome.scope: The three findings that stand today (the Service selector, the gate's answers, the Service half of the sequence) are the delivered scope; the two that wait on dispatch://INFRA-221 need an owner named.
